```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, dpi = 80)
```

Porreca, Maturo and Ventre (2025) define fuzzy degree, closeness and
betweenness for directed networks whose ties are triangular fuzzy numbers
(TFNs). The crisp formula is applied to the three parameters of the TFNs,
intermediate choices (the order of the ties in an ordered weighted average,
the best path between two actors) are made by ranking TFNs through their centre
of gravity (CoG), and actors are ranked by the CoG of their fuzzy centrality.
This vignette describes the functions that implement these indices. The exact
fuzzy centrality defined by the extension principle, developed in Porreca and
Maturo (2026), is described in `vignette("exact-centrality")`.

The examples use a simulated survey network (`?fsn_simulated`).

```{r}
library(FSNA)
A <- fsn_simulated()
```

## Degree

The fuzzy in- and out-degree are fuzzy triangular ordered weighted averages
(FTOWA) of the $n-1$ ties of an actor, computed with TFN arithmetic after
ordering the ties by their CoG. With equal weights the order of the ties does
not matter: the fuzzy degree is the in- or out-strength divided by $n-1$, and
coincides with the extension principle.

```{r}
print(ijar_degree(A, "in"), n = 5)
print(ijar_degree(A, "out"), n = 5)
```

With unequal weights the ties are ordered by their CoG, and the result can
differ from the extension of the OWA operator:

```{r}
a <- tfn(c(0, 0.3), c(0.2, 0.31), c(1, 0.32))
ftowa(a, "max")
owa_extension(a, c(1, 0))
```

## Closeness

A path is evaluated by its weakest tie, and the best path from one actor to
another is the path whose weakest tie is the strongest, with ties and paths
compared through their CoG. The fuzzy in-closeness of an actor is the average of
the strengths of the best paths, with at most $s$ steps, that reach it from the
other actors; the out-closeness uses the best paths that start from it.

```{r}
print(ijar_closeness(A, "in", max_steps = 2), n = 5)
print(ijar_closeness(A, "out", max_steps = 2), n = 5)
```

The strength of a path taken as the TFN of its weakest tie identified by CoG
differs from the extension of the minimum, which takes the minimum separately
on the left endpoints, the cores and the right endpoints:

```{r}
p <- tfn(c(0.1, 0.3), c(0.5, 0.45), c(0.9, 0.5))
path_strength(p, "weakest")
path_strength(p, "extension")
```

## Betweenness

Betweenness is the proportion of best paths between other actors that pass
through an actor, and is a crisp number; tied best paths share the count.

```{r}
print(ijar_betweenness(A), n = 5)
```

## Other ranking methods

Every function accepts `rank_method`, used to order the ties, select the best
paths and rank the actors:

```{r}
r <- sapply(fuzzy_rank_methods(), function(m) {
  d <- ijar_closeness(A, "in", rank_method = m)
  d$actor[order(d$rank)][1:5]
})
r
```

## Alternative computational choices

The indices depend on choices that the definitions leave to the analyst: the
strength assigned to a path, the treatment of paths with equal score, the
normalization and, for betweenness, the comparison of an indirect route with the
direct tie. `variant = "definition"`, the default, follows the definitions of
Section 3 of the paper. `variant = "alternative"`, defined for at most two
steps, takes the componentwise mean of the ties of a best path as its strength,
prefers indirect paths when scores are equal and divides closeness once more by
$n-1$. Each choice can also be set individually, which shows how much the
ranking of the actors depends on it.

```{r}
def <- ijar_closeness(A, "in")
alt <- ijar_closeness(A, "in", variant = "alternative")
mean_only <- ijar_closeness(A, "in", path_tfn = "mean")
c(alternative = cor(def$score, alt$score, method = "kendall"),
  mean_path = cor(def$score, mean_only$score, method = "kendall"))
```

## Exact counterpart

The exact fuzzy closeness with the minimum t-norm is the extension of the
best-path closeness; its triangle on the endpoints coincides with it at the
support and at the core (Porreca and Maturo, 2026).

```{r}
fc <- fuzzy_centrality(A, "in_closeness_min", max_steps = 2)
plot(fc, actors = 5)
```
